content.overview: BNS s. 71 — Punishment for repeat offenders.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Punishment for repeat offenders. BNS restatement of IPC 376E. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 376E. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 71 is the rule on “Punishment for repeat offenders”. The section provides that whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 64 or section 65 or section 66 or section 70 and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 71 exists so that “Punishment for repeat offenders” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
71. Whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 64 or section 65 or section 66 or section 70 and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 71 (Punishment for repeat offenders), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 64 or section 65 or section 66 or section 70 and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 71 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.

learningObjectives: Understand the enhanced penalty regime for recidivist sexual offenders under BNS s. 71.
Examine the mandatory sentence: imprisonment for remainder of natural life, or death.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 71 provides that whoever, having been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 64 or section 65 or section 66 or section 70, is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, or with death.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Recidivism in sexual violence demonstrates incorrigible dangerousness. A repeat offender convicted for a second or subsequent time of rape or gang rape faces mandatory life imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, or the death penalty.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 71 (corresponding to IPC s. 376E).
Prerequisite: Prior conviction under s. 64, 65, 66, or 70.
Trigger: Subsequent conviction under any of the said sections.
Mandatory sentence: Imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life), OR DEATH.
essentialIngredients: The accused has a prior final conviction under s. 64, 65, 66, or 70.
The accused commits a subsequent offence under any of those sections.
The court imposes natural-life imprisonment or death.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 71 targets chronic sexual predators. If an individual has served a sentence for rape under s. 64, and upon release commits another rape or gang rape, the court's sentencing discretion is restricted to the two most severe penalties recognized by law: imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, or capital punishment. The section requires proof of prior conviction in accordance with BNSS procedures (producing certified copy of previous conviction).
examples: Teaching example (Repeat rape conviction): An accused was convicted of rape under s. 64 in 2025 and served ten years. In 2035, he commits another rape. Upon conviction, s. 71 applies automatically; the court must sentence him to natural life imprisonment or death.
Teaching example (Prior conviction under IPC): Previous convictions under corresponding IPC sections (ss. 376, 376A, 376D) are recognized under transition and General Clauses principles.
distinctions: Section 71 vs Section 9 (General enhanced punishment for repeat property/coinage offenders): Section 71 is an exclusive, severe recidivism provision for sexual crimes carrying death or natural life.
Judicial discretion: The court's discretion is confined to choosing between natural life and death.
problemApplication: Issue: What sentence must be awarded to an accused who, having previously been convicted of gang rape, is subsequently convicted of raping an adult woman?
Rule: Under BNS s. 71, a person previously convicted under s. 70 who is subsequently convicted under s. 64 must be sentenced to natural life imprisonment or death.
Application: Certified record of previous conviction under s. 70 is placed on record. The subsequent conviction under s. 64 is established.
Conclusion: The court must sentence the convict to imprisonment for the remainder of natural life or death.

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 71 rule on repeat sexual offenders.
